claims.text: Rapid quenching of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 at 10^5–10^6 K/s can produce an amorphous structure.
The amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy is prone to primary crystallization during subsequent thermal processing.
A brief isothermal hold at approximately 0.8 Tg during reheating will suppress crystalline-phase nucleation and growth.
The proposed treatment consists of adding a short isothermal hold at approximately 0.8 Tg to the reheating sequence.
The proposed processing sequence includes rapid quenching followed by a slower-cooling segment before reheating.
At approximately 0.8 Tg, atomic mobility is sufficient to relieve internal stresses and permit structural relaxation.
At approximately 0.8 Tg, the thermal energy remains insufficient to overcome the alloy's crystallization barrier.
Stress relief and structural relaxation without barrier crossing will retard primary crystallization and stabilize the amorphous phase.
The isothermal hold will delay the onset of exothermic crystallization peaks during DSC reheating.
The isothermal hold will reduce the intensity of exothermic crystallization peaks during DSC reheating.
The isothermal hold will increase the retained amorphous fraction and thermal stability relative to reheating without a hold.
Standard reheating without an isothermal hold typically produces pronounced primary crystallization and reduced amorphous retention.
The intervention's effectiveness may diminish below 0.7 Tg or above 0.9 Tg.
The hold duration must be optimized to balance structural relaxation against crystallization kinetics.
The optimal hold duration and temperature may vary with small changes in composition or processing conditions.
